take: US crude imports from Venezuela averaged 701,000 b/d in July, the highest since May 2017 before easing to 655,000 b/d in August, which matters because it adds heavy sour supply into the US Gulf Coast at a time when refiners are already running above 95% utilisation between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. The more important signal is the yield shift: exceptionally high distillate and jet margins have pulled refinery output away from gasoline towards middle distillates, so the product complex is where the tightness sits rather than at the crude end. On freight, oil traders are lobbying Washington to release sanctioned tankers as a global vessel shortage pushes transportation costs to extraordinary levels, and with the shipbuilding orderbook up three and a half times since 2020 against only 30% yard capacity growth, the delivery crunch into 2028 keeps tanker earnings structurally bid. The inventory angle is thin on hard numbers today, but the Q2 global refinery run cut of 4.8 million b/d, or 6%, following the late-February Middle East conflict implies a drawdown that has not been fully rebuilt, so any crude length is likely sitting in floating or sanctioned tonnage rather than onshore. Cross-market, watch the gasoil-bunker spread: distillate-led refinery economics support middle distillate cracks whilst HSFO availability hinges on whether sanctioned barrels return to service, and a 15-month suezmax charter worth $73.1m to $82.2m shows owners are locking in elevated rates rather than betting on spot. For the next 24 hours, track any US signal on sanctioned tanker releases, the COP31 electrification narrative for medium-term gasoil demand destruction, and the IEA warning that the global gas market could stay tight well into 2027, which keeps the gas-to-oil switching tail alive.

items.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
items.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Colombia's government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought resulting from an expected strong El Niño.

items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026

Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
